name: Modal Verbs
description: Ability, permission, obligation, prohibition, advice and deduction, including perfect modals and modal alternatives.

questions.title: You ___ wear a helmet on a building site. It is the law.
___ I borrow your dictionary for a moment?
She ___ swim when she was four years old.
You ___ take photographs inside the gallery. It is forbidden.
You look tired. You ___ go to bed earlier.
It is Sunday, so we ___ get up early.
Which sentence expresses a strong deduction?
options: The lights are on, so he must be at home.
The lights are on, so he can be at home.
The lights are on, so he should be at home.
The lights are on, so he would be at home.

questions.title: What form follows a modal verb?
___ you help me carry these boxes, please?
He ___ be at work, because his car is still in the drive.
Which sentence gives advice most gently?
options: You might want to check the timetable.
You have to check the timetable.

questions.title: We ___ to submit the form by Friday.
Which modal is used for a polite offer in a shop?
Dogs ___ be kept on a lead in the park.
Match each modal verb with the meaning it expresses.
Match each sentence with the function it performs.
pairs: You must not open the window.

questions.title: Match each negative form with its meaning.
pairs: it is not a good idea

questions.title: Match each situation with the modal that fits it.
pairs: Excuse me, could you tell me the way?
warning a child near a road
You must not run into the street.
giving a friend advice about revision
You should start a week earlier.
saying an exam is not compulsory
You don't have to sit the second paper.

questions.title: The keys are not on the hook, so somebody ___ them.
She ___ the message, otherwise she would have replied.
You ___ told me the meeting was cancelled. I waited an hour.
I ___ have locked the door, but I honestly cannot remember.
Which sentence criticises a past action?
options: You shouldn't have spoken to her like that.
You mustn't speak to her like that.
You needn't speak to her like that.
You can't speak to her like that.

questions.title: We ___ have booked in advance; the restaurant was half empty.
What is the difference between 'must' and 'have to'?
options: 'Must' often reflects the speaker's own authority; 'have to' reflects external rules.
'Must' is always about the past and 'have to' about the future.
'Must' is informal and 'have to' is formal.
There is no difference in modern English.

questions.title: When I was a student I ___ share a room with three other people.
He ___ be older than forty; he was still at school in 2015.
Which sentence expresses a past ability that was actually used on one occasion?
options: She managed to persuade the committee.

questions.title: You ___ worry about the results; they are not published until June.
Passengers ___ remain seated until the aircraft comes to a complete stop.
Students ___ use dictionaries during the listening paper.
Match each perfect modal with the meaning it carries.
pairs: a confident conclusion about the past
a criticism of what was not done

questions.title: Match each modal expression with a synonym of the same strength.
Match each sentence with the exact nuance it carries.
pairs: you came, but it was unnecessary

questions.title: Match each degree of certainty with the modal that expresses it.
pairs: almost certain that it is true
almost certain that it is false

questions.title: Match each rule with the way it is normally worded in a public notice.
pairs: Helmets must be worn at all times.
Tickets need not be shown on this route.
Visitors are asked to keep their voices down.

questions.title: You ___ have waited for me; I told you I would be late.
Which sentence expresses a reproach about an unrealised past opportunity?
options: You could have applied for that scholarship.
You can apply for that scholarship.
You must have applied for that scholarship.
You had to apply for that scholarship.

questions.title: Whatever the outcome, the committee ___ be seen to act impartially.
Which sentence uses 'should' with its subjunctive meaning?
options: It is essential that every applicant should submit two references.
It is essential that every applicant should be submitting references.
It is essential that every applicant must submitting references.
It is essential that every applicant will submit references.

questions.title: He would rather we ___ the matter in public.
Which sentence is the most tentative?
options: The results might conceivably be affected by the sample size.
The results must be affected by the sample size.
The results will be affected by the sample size.
The results are affected by the sample size.

questions.title: Match each formal modal expression with its everyday equivalent.
pairs: Visitors may wish to book ahead.
It is a good idea to book.
Under no circumstances may the door be opened.
Candidates need not bring a calculator.

questions.title: Match each modal pattern with the meaning it adds.
pairs: would have been expected to attend

questions.title: Match each sentence with the attitude the speaker signals.
pairs: I dare say she was right.
I would go so far as to say she was right.
She may have had a point.
She could scarcely have been more wrong.
